images.canvas: IIIF canvas index 103 (image corner marked folio 101)
images.shows: Full-page nomenclator/Polybius-style cipher table in a later (post-Sarpi) hand: hundreds of code-word/number pairs organised alphabetically (city and office names visible: Bruxelles, Anversa, Milano, Roma, Firenze...), a 'nulle a.e.i.o.u.' null-letter line. The facing canvas (index 102, folio 100, not saved) carries only a French heading note: 'Chiffre escrit de la main du Pere Paul par lequel il se servoit avec ses amys auquel il a joint les lettres italiennes qu'on peut au reste de ce volume.'

images.canvas: IIIF canvas index 36 (approx. folio 34, matching Busnelli's citation 'Dupuy 111, f.34r-v' for the 16 Feb 1610 letter to Castrino)
images.shows: An actual enciphered letter: continuous Italian prose with two- and three-digit numeral groups embedded inline in place of names/places (nomenclator over cleartext connective prose), addressed on the facing leaf 'Al molto Ill.re Sig.r ... il Signor [addressee name obscured]'. Confirms the volume DOES contain real ciphertext, not only the key.

note: f100-101 (the key, per the BnF catalogue's 'f.100') sit near the END of Sarpi's autograph run (105 leaves total), not the head; the letters proper (dated Oct 1608-July 1617 to 'Castrino') run through earlier folios, at least one of which (~f.34) is genuinely enciphered.
